review_evidence: README describes the repository as an extensive coherent library of formalized mathematical theories used by major formal proofs.
Primary .v files define structures and prove lemmas throughout boot, ssreflect, algebra, field, group, and related packages.
Sampled field/qfpoly.v, field/closed_field.v, field/falgebra.v, and field/algC.v show reusable definitions and theorem infrastructure rather than scaffolding.
summary: Retain MathComp: the core Mathematical Components library is an extensive reusable Rocq formalization spanning data structures, algebra, finite groups, fields, and supporting theory.

review_evidence: No 'Exclusions already in force' section is present in brief RRU-d2568c3b8e8b.md (confirmed by a full read of the brief and a targeted grep for that heading, which returned no match).

Ran a Rocq declaration-marker grep (Theorem|Lemma|Definition|Fixpoint|Inductive|Record|Instance|Module|Axiom|Class|Notation|Tactic|Ltac|Corollary|Remark, unanchored) across all 3 files: algebra/arithmetic_tactic.v 132, algebra/field_tactic.v 107, algebra/ring_tactic.v 198 -- all well above zero.

Read the header (first ~40 lines) of each of the 3 files: algebra/arithmetic_tactic.v documents the `lra`, `nra`, `psatz`/`psatz n` decision procedures for linear/nonlinear real arithmetic (Positivstellensatz-based, optional CSDP solver) over realDomainType/realFieldType, handling additive and ring morphisms; algebra/field_tactic.v documents the `field`/`field by <tac>`/`field?`/`field[?]: e1..en` tactics for field equalities over fieldType by normalizing to a pair of polynomials; algebra/ring_tactic.v documents the `ring`/`ring: e1..en` tactic for (semi)ring equalities over comRingType/comSemiRingType by polynomial normalization. Each is built on the mathcomp `elpi`/`micromega_plugin` infrastructure and contains its own Notation, Tactic Notation, and Ltac/Lemma declarations implementing and specifying the decision procedure -- these are core reusable MathComp automation modules, not build/CI/meta tooling, and the tactics' documented semantics plus their declarations are exactly the kind of formal-mathematics interface the corpus indexes.

All 3 files score well above zero on the declaration-marker grep and their headers confirm substantive, non-generated formal content; no file was proposed for exclusion so no full read beyond the headers was required.
